subject: DPA: purge evidence matrix and operational playbook — clarifications
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: DPA scope — purge evidence + timeline questions

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. Our security and legal teams have a few follow-ups after reviewing the DPA draft. Key asks:
- We need an "evidence matrix" that maps each retention tier (prod, logs, backups, ephemeral caches) to what proof Redwood can provide when data is purged (certificates, sha256, audit logs, deletion ticket IDs).
- Can Redwood commit to a notification and a signed deletion certificate after a scheduled purge, and what is the max wait time to receive that certificate?
- Backups: what's your operational SLA for removing data from snapshots/replicas once a deletion request is processed? We understand restore windows — need clarity on maximum latency.
- Legal hold carve-outs: if a hold is raised, what is the preservation workflow and how is the hold surfaced to customers?

I've attached our initial request summary (initial-request.pdf). If you can provide the evidence matrix and a proposed playbook for scheduled purge notifications, we can mark this as ready for our legal redline pass.

Appreciate it — can we aim to have a draft by end of week?

—Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Security Programs
Acme Corporation
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA scope — purge evidence + timeline questions

Sarah — thanks, received and copied legal/infra. Quick acknowledgements:
- We can produce a per-purge artifact containing (a) purge ticket ID, (b) timestamp, (c) list of deleted object ids, and (d) an HMAC/sha256 signed by Redwood's key. We call this the "Deletion Certificate."
- Backups and snapshot windows vary by product tier; we can outline maximum removal timelines per tier in the evidence matrix.
- Legal holds: Redwood supports a hold flag that prevents destruction; the hold lifecycle is surfaced via the Console and via audit logs. We will describe escalation steps in the playbook.

Marissa / Karthik — can you draft a short evidence matrix and a 1–page operational playbook (scheduled purge -> certificate -> verification steps) that we can share back to Acme? Sarah, we'll attach a redline to the DPA with those elements.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA scope — purge evidence + timeline questions

Jonas / Karthik,

Drafted an initial legal-side response and attached a tracked redline (redwood_dpa_redline_v3.docx). Highlights for the evidence matrix:
- Tier A (production customer data): Deletion Certificate delivered within 7 business days of purge job completion; backups best-effort removal within 90 days, with a monthly snapshot sweep cadence (we include exception language for cold-archive / regulated-subpoena retention).
- Tier B (non-PII telemetry/logs): Certificate within 14 business days; backups 30–60 days depending on retention TTL.
- Tier C (ephemeral caches / KV): Immediate TTL eviction; certificate posted via API within 48 hours for triggered deletes.

Proposed contract language for legal holds: customer must submit a signed hold notice; Redwood will suspend purge jobs for affected tenant IDs and mark evidence certificates as "withheld due to legal hold". We also propose an attestation clause for periodic audit access (SOC2 / porovided logs) rather than wholesale deletion proofs for archived cold stores.

Karthik — please add any operational constraints (snapshot replication lag, replica cleanup cadence) so I can insert them into the redline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA scope — purge evidence + timeline questions

Marissa, thanks — couple quick clarifications from our side:
- 7 business days for a production Deletion Certificate is acceptable, but we need a guarantee that the certificate includes a signed digest (SHA256) and Redwood's certificate chain so our auditors can validate authenticity.
- The 90-day backup removal window: can we narrow that to 60 days for Tier A if we accept a staggered SLA (e.g., critical partitions within 30 days, full wipe within 60)? Our compliance team will push back on 90 days if we don't get faster assurances for the hot replica sets.
- Regarding holds: the signed hold notice is fine — can Redwood expose an API endpoint to check hold status and expected release date? That is a hard requirement for our orchestration.

If you can tweak the redline to reflect the SHA256 + cert chain requirement, and a proposed 30/60 fallback for critical partitions vs full backup sweep, we can escalate to our GC for sign-off.

Thanks,
—Sarah
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA scope — purge evidence + timeline questions

Sarah — technical notes and proposed operational language for the playbook:
- Deletion Certificate contents: ticket_id, tenant_id, object_list (IDs), purge_timestamp (UTC), SHA256 digest over the object_list + timestamp, Redwood signing cert fingerprint. We can provide the cert chain via the Console or as a downloadable PEM.
- Backups: for hot replica sets we can commit to a 30-day targeted purge on affected partitions, then 60-day full snapshot lifecycle for the tenant (we'll document exact sweep windows and provide a retention calendar). Cold-archive exemptions will be explicit in the DPA appendix.
- API: we will expose an authenticated endpoint (/api/v1/holds/{tenant_id}) returning hold status, raising_time, expected_release (nullable). We'll include rate limits and RBAC guidance.
- Operational playbook steps (high level): receive deletion request -> validate tenant scope -> schedule purge job -> run purge -> create Deletion Certificate -> push certificate to Console + email to customer contact -> queue backup sweep -> mark ticket resolved.

Next steps: I'll update the evidence_matrix.xlsx with the timelines and add the API spec stub. Marissa, please accept those small language tweaks if they match the redline. Jonas — can you propose a 30-minute working session with Acme legal/security to walk through the matrix and certificate format?

Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference
